source.sourceText: Wake up at 7 AM after setting alarm
Opa sits up in bed, staring at a bedside clock whose hour hand is moving backward past 6, while the alarm hand points to 7.
The clock's hands move backward whenever the alarm is set, so time appears to run in reverse; the alarm rings only when the hands return to midnight.
Opa sets alarm for 7:00, the hour hand starts cranking counterclockwise.

Opa Opa turns the alarm off and just watches the clock to see what time it shows.. The hands freeze, then twitch backward one minute for every real second that passes. Without alarm set, the clock still runs backward but slower.

Opa Opa sets the alarm for a time that already appears behind the current hand position, like 2:00, hoping it will trigger quickly.. The alarm rings immediately, but the hands jump forward to noon, and the ringing reverses itself into a silent vacuum of sound. Triggering the alarm causes time to jump forward to noon and sound to invert.

Opa Opa unplugs the clock and uses his phone to check the actual time.. The clock's display reappears on his phone screen, showing the same backward time, and the phone's alarm icon turns into an hourglass. The clock's impossible rule spreads to other time-keeping devices.

Opa Opa gives up and falls back asleep.. The clock chimes twelve times in reverse, and Opa wakes up at 7 AM, but the clock reads 7 PM. The backward time eventually catches up to the correct wake hour, but day and night are swapped.
